headline: Barclays cuts 5,000 jobs with AI as a driver, EA shuts BioWare and cancels the next Mass Effect, Capcom leaks 11.8 million account records, and the ICC wins the Sakharov Prize.

stories.title: Barclays is cutting 5,000 jobs, about 5% of staff, and credits AI
facts: About 1,000 of the roles are already gone; the other 4,000 go before the end of the year.
Roughly 60% of the cuts hit support functions, including developers; most fall in the UK.
CFO Anna Cross tied the cuts to a plan to save more than £1.1bn in 2027.
CEO C.S. Venkatakrishnan called AI "the icing on the cake", not the cake: the gains come from years of infrastructure work.
Q3 profit was £2.3bn, up on the year but below forecasts as fixed-income trading underperformed.
stories.whyItMatters: One of the clearest cases yet of a big bank putting a number on AI-linked job cuts, and it explicitly includes developer roles.

stories.title: EA shuts down BioWare and cancels the next Mass Effect
facts: EA is closing BioWare and its Edmonton office; a small team there was in early development on the next Mass Effect, which is cancelled.
About 400 jobs go, roughly 3% of EA's staff, also at Ripple Effect, Maxis and Skate studio Full Circle.
It's EA's first big move since going private in its $55bn sale to a group led by Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund.
EA also paused a mobile multiplayer Sims game, has Respawn and DICE teaming up on Star Wars: Battlefront 3, and says Fight Night is coming back.
stories.whyItMatters: BioWare made Baldur's Gate, KOTOR, Mass Effect and Dragon Age; its closure signals the new owners are betting on fewer, bigger franchises.

stories.title: Capcom says 11.77 million CAPCOM ID records were accessed
facts: 11,774,247 records with email addresses, account creation and last-login times, login counts and last-login IP were exposed.
For 43 accounts, birth date, gender, country and nickname leaked too; 196 accounts had their passwords changed by the attacker and have been reset.
Capcom says original passwords and credit-card data weren't affected; it spotted the access on 19 October and reported it to police on 21 October.
It warns of phishing mails pretending to be Capcom.
stories.whyItMatters: If you have a CAPCOM ID (for example for Street Fighter 6), expect convincing phishing to your registered address.

stories.title: The EU Parliament gives the Sakharov Prize to the sanctioned International Criminal Court
facts: Parliament President Roberta Metsola announced the award in Strasbourg; it honours the court and its officials.
It comes weeks after the US imposed new ICC sanctions and moved to freeze the court's US assets.
Other finalists were Tanzanian opposition leader Tundu Lissu and Taraneh and Romina Rahimi for those persecuted by Iran's regime.
The €50,000 prize will be presented on 16 December.

facts.text: Meta faces an Australian class action in the Federal Court on behalf of children allegedly harmed by Facebook and Instagram; Meta says it will defend itself vigorously.
Saxony-Anhalt: ex-CDU group leader Guido Heuer says he won't leave the chamber when AfD's Ulrich Siegmund stands for premier in December, breaking with his group's walkout plan.
Fortnite is back on Apple's App Store in Australia after a federal court ordered Apple to open iOS to competition.
Chiricahua in Arizona, a sacred Apache site, is now the 64th US national park.
Eintracht Braunschweig: Hildesheim police took down about 40 "Eintracht verrecke" posters ahead of Sunday's derby against Hannover but found nothing criminal in them.
Bun v1.4.4 is out: 271 issues fixed, a Prettier-compatible `bun fmt`, `bun check` 1.4x to 7.8x faster, and security fixes including Brotli and TLS certs.
Bun also merged a change so node:http and node:http2 refuse the malformed requests Node refuses.
OpenAI has an official Go CLI for its REST API (`openai/openai-cli`), covering Responses, image and speech generation, and Admin API key management.
Status pages flagged elevated ChatGPT and Responses API errors at OpenAI and connector errors at Anthropic this morning.
Perplexity Computer can now run fully on a Mac with Qwen 3.6, no cloud needed (heise).
